references.text: Shortly before this verse, Jesus says that the kingdom of God does not come in such a way that one can say, "Look, here it is!" or "There it is!" ([ref:Luk 17:21|Luke 17:21]). Verse 23 repeats and expands on this warning in the context of the day of the Son of Man.

Jesus warns the disciples against following false leaders who say, "The time is near" – the same type of warning against being misled by false claims about the coming of the Messiah ([ref:Luk 21:8|Luke 21:8]).

The parallel in Matthew where Jesus gives the same warning: "If anyone says to you then, 'Look, here is the Messiah' or 'There he is,' do not believe it!" and explains that false messiahs and false prophets will appear ([ref:Matt 24:23-26|Matthew 24:23-26]).

The parallel in Mark where Jesus warns against those who say, "Look, here is the Messiah" or "Look, there he is", and that false messiahs and false prophets will appear with signs and wonders to lead people astray ([ref:Mark 13:21-23|Mark 13:21-23]).

Right after the warning in Matthew, Jesus explains that the coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning – visible to all – so there is no need to look for him in specific places ([ref:Matt 24:27|Matthew 24:27]). This expands on the reason for the warning in Luke 17:23.

The next verse explains why one should not run after such claims: the day of the Son of Man will be like lightning that shines from one end of heaven to the other – it will be unmistakable ([ref:Luk 17:24|Luke 17:24]).

Already in the Mosaic Law, there is a warning against false prophets who seek to lead the people to follow other gods. The principle of not following misleading voices is deeply rooted in the OT ([ref:5 Mos 13:2-4|Deuteronomy 13:2-4]).

John urges believers not to believe every spirit, but to test the spirits to see if they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world ([ref:1 Joh 4:1|1 John 4:1]). The same warning against being led astray by false claims.
